title: Committee of Supply − Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)

sections.label: Bangladeshi men detained under ISA
sections.summary: Eight radicalised Bangladeshi men were detained under the ISA for plotting terror attacks in their own country, and five others investigated were repatriated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In May 2016, it was revealed that "eight radicalised Bangladeshi men were detained under the Internal Security Act (ISA) for plotting terror attacks in their own country, that they would meet in parks or open fields and share large amounts of radical propaganda and videos." Another five investigated under the ISA were repatriated.

sections.label: Indonesian police foil rocket plan
sections.summary: In August 2016, Indonesian police foiled a plan for a rocket attack on Marina Bay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In August 2016, the Indonesian police foiled the plan for a rocket attack on Marina Bay.

sections.label: Update sought on terror measures
sections.summary: A Member seeks an update on how MHA tracks overseas terror threats, isolates internal threats, reinforces enforcement and bolsters communal response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, as recent as this week, I read that a Police report was made about an imam who was alleged to have made offensive remarks against Christians and Jews.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In light of these challenges, I seek an update from the good Minister, in particular, how is the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA): one, tracking overseas terror threats; two, isolating potential threats from within Singapore society; three, reinforcing our enforcement response, such as manpower, equipment and the updating of our standard operating procedures against such threats; four, bolstering our communal response by strengthening multiracialism and national unity should a terror threat vest in Singapore.

sections.label: Population centres as soft targets
sections.summary: Many population centres such as schools, shopping centres, transport stations and hospitals are soft targets for those seeking to do harm.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Many population centres happen to be soft targets for those seeking to do us harm, such as schools with young children, shopping centres with members of the public, Mass Rapid Transit and bus stations which, if shut down, could affect a wide transport network and even our hospitals, with the sick and elderly who cannot be evacuated as easily as the able-bodied.

sections.label: Boon Lay SGSecure ambassadors recruited
sections.summary: About 500 SGSecure ambassadors were recruited in Boon Lay last November and training is expected this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In my Boon Lay constituency, we have recruited about 500 SGSecure ambassadors last November and look forward to training them this year.

sections.label: C2E and IRCC terror exercises
sections.summary: C2E Committees and IRCCs held exercises on handling days after a terror attack, but roles were not clearly delineated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Community Emergency and Engagement Committees (C2E Committees) and the Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs) have undergone some exercises to learn about handling the situation in the days following a terror attack.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: One, the exercises were done separately for the C2E committees and IRCCs but there was overlap in the grassroots leaders and community organisations involved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The exercises were also similar and there did not appear to be a clear delineation of the roles the different committees play.

sections.label: Reviewing grading exercise timelines
sections.summary: Suggests PLRD review timelines between grading exercises, noting most of the 250 agencies are small and medium enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Considering that most of the 250 agencies are small and medium enterprises, perhaps the Police Licensing and Regulatory Department (PLRD) can look at reviewing the timelines in between the grading exercises.

sections.label: Singapore population growth figures
sections.summary: States Singapore's population is now more than 5.6 million, up 1.2 million from 4.4 million in 2006.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The population of Singapore is now more than 5.6 million, compared to 4.4 million in 2006, a 1.2 million increase over 10 years.

sections.label: Certis Cisco Taiwan recruitment approval
sections.summary: The Minister confirmed Certis Cisco obtained approval to recruit officers from Taiwan due to manpower shortages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In answer to a Parliamentary Question I filed, the Minister has confirmed that Certis Cisco has obtained approval to recruit officers from Taiwan due to manpower shortages.

sections.label: Initiative put on hold
sections.summary: A Parliamentary answer last October said the Government put the initiative on hold pending a legal framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Last October, I was disappointed to learn from a Parliamentary answer that the Government had decided to put the initiative on hold, pending putting the legal framework in place.

sections.label: CYPA age gap and CRC
sections.summary: Argues the CYPA's age definitions leave 16 to 18 year olds unprotected, inconsistent with CRC obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under Article 4 of CRC, Singapore is obliged to undertake all appropriate legislative, administrative and other measures for the implementation of the rights recognised in the Convention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, Madam Chair, our Children and Young Persons Act (CYPA) defines a child to be a person below the age of 14 and a young person to be between the ages of 14 and 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, children in Singapore between 16 and 18 years old are not protected by section 35 of the CYPA which prevents the media from publishing their particulars or identifying details of those under 16 years old involved in Court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This gap in our law is not consistent with our CRC obligations as Article 40 obliges state parties to ensure that every child up to the age of 18 has his/her privacy fully respected during criminal proceedings.

sections.label: Appropriate Adult scheme questions
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will entrench and extend the Appropriate Adult scheme and admit parents as Appropriate Adults.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Otherwise, what is the point of signing this treaty?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope the Ministry will have a legislative framework to entrench the Appropriate Adult scheme and extend it to those below 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry also consider admitting parents of such suspects to act as Appropriate Adults?

sections.label: Inmate training and work declines
sections.summary: In 2014 and 2015 inmate training numbers fell 7% and 6% while work programme engagement fell 4%, despite only a 1% drop in total inmates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2014 to 2015, despite only a 1% decline in the total number of inmates, there was a 7% decline in the number of inmates trained in 2014 and a 6% decline in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There was also a 4% decline in the number of inmates engaged in work programmes.

sections.label: Recidivism and drug repeat offenders
sections.summary: Recidivism stayed around 26%, almost 60% of arrested drug abusers were repeat offenders, and more incarcerations for drug offences raised the chances of re-incarceration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While the recidivism rate has remained stable at around 26%, it is worrying to me that almost 60% of drug abusers arrested were repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Even more worrying is that statistics that the more times we incarcerate someone for drug offences, the higher the chances he or she will be incarcerated again.

sections.label: DRC inmates' visit quota use
sections.summary: Only a third of DRC inmates use their full quota of two 30-minute visits per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Only a third of DRC inmates use their full quota of two 30-minute visits per month.

sections.label: Online drug arrests rise
sections.summary: Arrests for buying drugs and drug-related paraphernalia online rose from 30 in 2015 to 201 in 2016, mostly people aged 20 to 39.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In fact, the number of people arrested for buying drugs and drug-related paraphernalia online increased significantly from just 30 in 2015 to 201 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Most of those found to have obtained drugs or drug-related paraphernalia online were between the ages of 20 and 39.

sections.label: Online drug arrests six-fold jump
sections.summary: The number of arrests for buying drugs and drug-related items online has jumped six-fold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The number of arrests for buying drugs and drug-related items online has jumped six-fold.

sections.label: Self-radicalised Singaporeans' arrests
sections.summary: The arrests of self-radicalised Singaporeans last year highlighted the danger of terrorist activities here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The arrests of self-radicalised Singaporeans last year highlighted the danger of terrorist activities here.

sections.label: Residents feel safe, Home Team confidence
sections.summary: Residents feel safe in their neighbourhoods and public confidence in the Home Team remained high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Overall, residents feel safe in their neighbourhoods and public confidence in the Home Team continued to be high.

sections.label: MHA budget cut and security
sections.summary: A question asks how safety and security are ensured with a 2% reduction in MHA's budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: With a 2% reduction in MHA's budget, how do we ensure that our safety and security are not compromised?

sections.label: National Service and Home Team clubhouses
sections.summary: Over 50 years, more than 260,000 men served or are serving NS with the Home Team, and three new clubhouses will be set up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over the past 50 years, more than 260,000 men have served National Service (NS) or are serving NS with the Home Team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Three new Home Team clubhouses will be set up within the next 10-15 years.

sections.label: Reducing remote or online gambling
sections.summary: A question asks what measures are taken to further reduce remote or online gambling given its destructive consequences for addicts' families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Given the destructive consequences problem gambling can bring to the family of a gambling addict, what measures are we taking to further reduce the incidence of remote or online gambling?

sections.label: Expediting sexual abuse investigations
sections.summary: A question asks whether investigations into sexual abuse against minors will be prioritised and expedited for the child and parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: This is because the parents do not want to prolong the anguish of the child and, also, the child may find it difficult to recount the evidence as time goes by.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Therefore, would the Minister direct their investigations into sexual abuse against minors be prioritised and expedited for the sake of the child and the parents?

sections.label: Crime rate and Gallup ranking
sections.summary: The overall crime rate in 2016 was the lowest in three years and Singapore ranked first in Gallup's Law and Order 2016 Report.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The overall crime rate in 2016 was the lowest in the last three years and we were again ranked first in the Gallup's Law and Order 2016 Report.

sections.label: Public rating of safety
sections.summary: 92% rated general safety and security in Singapore as good or very good.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: On the question of the public's sense of safety and security, 92% rated general safety and security in Singapore as "good" or "very good".

sections.label: Feeling safe at night
sections.summary: 93% felt safe walking in their neighbourhood at night, attributed to an effective Police Force, more Police presence and quick arrests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Ninety-three percent felt safe walking in their neighbourhood at night and that was attributed to a highly effective Police Force, more Police presence and, again, quick arrest of criminals.

sections.label: Police as world-class
sections.summary: 87% regarded the Police as a world-class crime fighting organisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Eighty-seven percent regarded the Police as a world-class crime fighting organisation.

sections.label: Terrorism threat remains high
sections.summary: The threat of terrorism continues to be high.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The threat of terrorism continues to be high.

sections.label: Militant groups and Singapore actions
sections.summary: In 2016 four militant groups formed the Islamic State Philippines and pledged allegiance to ISIS, which endorsed Isnilon Hapilon as Southeast Asia amir; Singapore took security action against nine Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2016, four militant groups established an umbrella group called the Islamic State Philippines (ISP) and pledged their allegiance to ISIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: ISIS also endorsed ISP leader, Isnilon Hapilon, a leader of the Abu Sayyaf Group in Basilan, as "amir", or supreme leader, for Southeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Within Singapore, we took security action against nine Singaporeans last year.

sections.label: Largest counterterrorism exercise
sections.summary: In October last year Singapore conducted its largest counterterrorism exercise to date, with more than 3,200 participants.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In October of last year, we conducted the largest counterterrorism exercise to date, involving more than 3,200 participants.

sections.label: Police Cameras Installation Plan
sections.summary: About 11,000 Police Cameras will be installed at 2,500 locations island-wide over the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Over the next few years, we will install about 11,000 Police Cameras at 2,500 locations island-wide.

sections.label: Religious Preaching and Action
sections.summary: A Christian couple was jailed in 2009 for anti-Islam publications; action depends on whether the imam made inflammatory suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2009, a Christian couple was sentenced to eight weeks' jail for distributing publications that cast Islam in a negative light.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The same applies to any attack on any other religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will not tolerate any religious preaching that encourages violence or seeks to pit one religion against another.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the imam had not made any inflammatory suggestion, no action will be taken and we will issue a public statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But if he did, indeed, make such suggestions or had engaged in such preaching, then some appropriate action will be taken.

sections.label: Live Exercises Rollout
sections.summary: Live exercises sensitise residents to attack threats and train responses, to be rolled out across all 89 constituencies over two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Live exercises sensitise residents to the threat of attacks and train their responses.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will roll it out across all 89 constituencies over the next two years.

sections.label: Opioid Abuse Deaths 2015
sections.summary: In 2015, more than 33,000 people died from opioid abuse, excluding drug-linked gun violence deaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2015, more than 33,000 people died from opioid abuse and that does not include the number who died due to gun-related violence but linked to drugs.

sections.label: Singapore Drug Problem Handling
sections.summary: Singapore is one of the few countries that has dealt effectively with the drug problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Singapore is one of the few countries in the world that has dealt effectively with the drug problem.

sections.label: Singapore Low Drug Consumption
sections.summary: It had to concede that Singapore's drug consumption is admirably low.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Yet, it had to concede that Singapore's drug consumption is admirably low.

sections.label: Myanmar and Laos opium cultivation
sections.summary: Myanmar and Lao PDR account for 22% of the global area used for illicit opium poppy cultivation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Myanmar and Lao PDR account for 22% of the total global area used for illicit opium poppy cultivation.

sections.label: New abusers under 30
sections.summary: Close to two-thirds of new abusers in 2016 were under the age of 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Close to two-thirds of new abusers in 2016 were under the age of 30.

sections.label: Extra time and implementation shift
sections.summary: Amrin Amin and the speaker seek Mdm Chair's indulgence for extra time, and this year they shift from planning to implementation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In order for Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin and I to address the remaining cuts, may we have Mdm Chair's indulgence for us to take that extra time?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This year, we are shifting gears significantly from planning to implementation.

sections.label: Co-locating departments' operation centres
sections.summary: By year's end, Police, CNB, SCDF and ICA officers will sit side-by-side at the Police Operations Command Centre for faster communication and coordination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For example, we are co-locating the various departments' operation centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, by the end of this year, officers from the Police, CNB, SCDF and ICA will sit side-by-side at the Police Operations Command Centre, enabling faster communication and information sharing and enhancing coordination of ground responses to incidents.

sections.label: Residents trained in CPR-AED
sections.summary: About 2,000 residents have been trained in CPR-AED skills under the Save-A-Life initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: About 2,000 residents have been trained in CPR-AED skills under the Save-A-Life initiative.

sections.label: AEDs for HDB blocks
sections.summary: By 2019, there will be one AED for every two HDB blocks in all constituencies across the island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: By 2019, there will be one AED for every two HDB blocks in all constituencies across the whole island.

sections.label: Businesses guarding against security threats
sections.summary: Laws will be amended this year to require businesses to adopt measures against security threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: (In English): Aside from individual citizens, businesses have an important role to play in Singapore's security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will amend our laws this year to require businesses to adopt certain measures to guard against security threats.

sections.label: Recruitment of foreign APOs
sections.summary: After considering options, it was decided to allow the recruitment of foreign APOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Do we live with the shortage of APOs and compromise on overall security when we need to deploy officers, or do we find other sources to meet these needs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have carefully considered the options and have decided to allow the recruitment of foreign APOs.

sections.label: Foreign APOs bearing arms
sections.summary: Non-Singaporean APOs, namely Malaysians, have carried arms since the 1970s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim was concerned about foreign APOs bearing arms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There are already, since the 1970s, non-Singaporean APOs carrying arms − these are the Malaysians.

sections.label: National Cybercrime Action Plan
sections.summary: MHA launched the National Cybercrime Action Plan last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Last year, MHA launched the National Cybercrime Action Plan.

sections.label: Safeguards for exempt operators
sections.summary: Singapore Pools and Singapore Turf Club, as exempt operators, must put in place an extensive suite of safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As exempt operators, Singapore Pools and Singapore Turf Club have to put in place a very extensive suite of safeguards.

sections.label: Legislative amendments before pilot
sections.summary: After consulting the legal community, it was decided to make legislative amendments before starting the pilot, with work ongoing, VRI-enabled interview rooms being configured and officer training enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Essentially, we have consulted the legal community and, after taking into account the feedback that they have given, we have decided it would be better to put in place the necessary legislative amendments before starting the pilot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The work to amend the legislation is ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We are also configuring VRI-enabled interview rooms for our law enforcement agencies and enhancing training for our officers.

sections.label: Youth Criminal Justice System review
sections.summary: MSF, MHA and AGC began a 2015 review of the youth Criminal Justice System, with recommendations the Government is studying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In October 2015, MSF, MHA and the Attorney-General's Chambers started a review of the Criminal Justice System for youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Committee has made several recommendations, including to further strengthen the protection of youth offenders between the ages of 16 and 18 and raising the threshold under CYPA to 18 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Government is presently studying the recommendations and will announce details in due course.

sections.label: Drug abusers arrested 2016
sections.summary: Drug abuser arrests fell 3% in 2016 from 2015, but close to two-thirds of new abusers were under 30, with more student cases.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: In 2016, there was a 3% drop in the number of drug abusers arrested compared to 2015, but there are areas of concern.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Close to two-thirds of the new drug abusers arrested were below the age of 30, and we are also seeing more cases of students abusing drugs.

sections.label: IMH cannabis review findings
sections.summary: An IMH expert review found cannabis harmful and addictive, with adolescent chronic exposure linked to lower IQ and possible lasting cognitive decline.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: A review conducted by experts at Singapore's IMH found that cannabis is both harmful and addictive, and chronic exposure to cannabis during adolescence is linked to lower intelligence quotient and possibly irreversible decline in cognitive performance lasting into adulthood.

sections.label: Man taught sons ice
sections.summary: He mixed with bad company, picked up drugs, never quit, and taught his two young sons aged 19 and 20 to smoke ice.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: He mixed with bad company, picked up drugs and never successfully quit.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: He taught his two young sons, aged 19 and 20, to smoke "ice".

sections.label: Day Release Scheme
sections.summary: Under the Day Release Scheme introduced last year, first-time lower-risk inmates can go out to work and study during the day.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Under the Day Release Scheme introduced last year, first-time lower-risk inmates can also go out to work and study during the day.

sections.label: Yellow Ribbon Community Project
sections.summary: The grassroots-led Yellow Ribbon Community Project helps inmates' families and children by connecting them to national social support networks, as family ties aid rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: The grassroots-led Yellow Ribbon Community Project (YRCP) was established to help the families and children of inmates cope by connecting them to the national social support networks.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: We recognise that family ties are vital to the inmates' rehabilitation, and family support is especially important after the inmates' release.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Thus, the community's long-term involvement is vital to ensure continuity in these efforts.

sections.label: WSQ training for inmates
sections.summary: SPS and SCORE run WSQ-aligned training, and SCORE will start WSQ Advanced Training for inmates during incarceration this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: SPS and SCORE conduct training programmes that are aligned with the Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: This year, SCORE will commence the WSQ Advanced Training for inmates during incarceration.

sections.label: Smart device courses for inmates
sections.summary: SCORE will introduce courses for inmates on using workplace smart devices such as tablets, to keep up with increased automation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: To keep up with increased automation in our workplaces, SCORE will introduce courses for inmates on the use of workplace smart devices, such as tablets.

sections.label: Inmates securing jobs before release
sections.summary: Over the last three years, more than 95% of inmates referred to SCORE secured jobs before release, helped by training and employer support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The combination of training and employer support have helped many inmates re-enter the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: And over the last three years, more than 95% of inmates referred to SCORE successfully secured jobs before their release.

sections.label: Skills upgrading for ex-offenders
sections.summary: In 2016 SCORE piloted sending well-performing ex-offenders for further skills upgrading, benefiting more than 260 ex-offenders so far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: In 2016, SCORE also worked with employers to pilot a new initiative where ex-offenders are sent for further skills upgrading if they perform well at work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: So far, more than 260 ex-offenders have benefited from this.

sections.label: Pilot with drug offenders
sections.summary: The programme will be piloted with about 100 drug offenders later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The programme will be piloted with about 100 drug offenders later this year.

sections.label: Home Team career transition programme
sections.summary: Police will introduce a structured career transition programme for retiring officers, with training time and course subsidies, and MHA may extend it to other Home Team departments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On his first question about older workers in the Home Team, the Police will be putting in place a more structured career transition programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It provides our retiring officers with dedicated training time as well as subsidies for them to take part in career transition courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Based on the outcome of these initiatives, MHA will also progressively extend these career transition support programmes to other Home Team departments.

sections.label: Home Team training modules
sections.summary: The Home Team Academy will roll out two new Home Team training modules later this year for new officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But to support this, you have to start from training, and officers need to go into their Home Team uniformed service knowing that they are part of a larger organisation and that they have to work together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, the Home Team Academy will be rolling out two new Home Team training modules later this year for our new officers.

sections.label: Video analytics for monitoring
sections.summary: They intend to enhance monitoring with video analytics because there are not enough officers to watch all the screens.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You mean whether it will move from pre-recorded to real-time monitoring?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We intend to go further and enhance these with video analytics capabilities, because we do not have the number of officers to watch all the thousands of screens.
